notes.title: Small Bug Fixes
notes.notes:
Just a small patch to fix the following bugs:

  It was possible to get 'The Adventure Begins' even if you were blocked from starting the game by not having a Trait or Heirloom selected.  The check for the achievement as before the check for the character customisation.  This has been corrected.
  People were not getting the extra skill bonus for the Beloved Locket when sleeping, unless they were also a doctor.  This was due to the checks to see if you had the item also included checks to make sure you were a doctor and had the Medical Kits to use.  This has been solved, and all sleeping related items/Traits should now work together as expected.

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 5
notes.notes:
Hope everyone is having a great week.  Here is the penultimate art page for you all to enjoy!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40946016/7c44bb5f6429ce3b384f2f1da2d65e160b18b6a1.jpg

Chalk Cove is also known as 'the city of steps'.  Even the interiors of the houses are laid out over multiple levels due to the steep incline the port is built into.  It is also frequently plague by mists.  Some say these are caused by the spirits of drowned sailors, who come back to the city for one last look at their old lives before moving on.

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 4
notes.notes:
Good morning!  Tattered Sails will be coming out this weekend, so as we come into the final countdown we have another art page to share.  Please enjoy your first glimpse of the Grass Sea.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40946016/3a33c33835cde69c47df6abfa8474ec0b02266e6.jpg

The whispering stalks of the Grass Sea hold many secrets.  Ghost towns and bandit camps, beast lairs and hidden temples.  Even with modern supplies the area is hard to navigate, and it is said that barely a third of the region has been fully mapped.  Who knows what wonders and horrors could be lurking behind the swaying plants?

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 3
notes.notes:
For today's art reveal we also have our second shout out in a row to Lovecraft Video Games.  They have posted a review of Tattered Sails which you can read here - https://www.lovecraftvideogames.com/delve-into-a-sinister-curse-in-the-hunters-journals-tattered-sails/  I am very glad that they liked this title, and I do hope people take their advice and use it as a means of getting into the series.  Don't forget to wishlist your copy today!

Below is our last art reveal for the week.  I am sure a lot of Red Ripper players would have loved to take several crates of this stuff with them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40946016/cf058568e5a987f4256374f11eb0a39c8bd336a1.jpg

Recent tales emerging from the Sunlight Alliance of rats the size of houses eating whole villages have led to an increase in sales of poisons like this.  A coincidentally rising statistic is the number of Broadsheet Killers who use these substances to commit their vile crimes.  Still, no giant rats have been sighted within the UIC's borders...yet.

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 2
notes.notes:
We're here to brighten up your Wednesday with another piece of stunning art by Muthur Brine.  And also to shout out to Lovecraft Video Games.  They spotted a bug while reviewing the game, and I was able to upload a fix last night thanks to them.  Check out their website (including reviews of all the Hunter's Journals to date) over at https://www.lovecraftvideogames.com/

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40946016/91d66a1aa14aa407810560eefbae58641dd2e0db.jpg

The box this bitter incense comes in claims it can keep spirits and minor Infernals at bay.  Rumour has it that the stuff also dismisses Externals who are exposed to the smoke.  The monastery which produces the cones make no such bold claim out loud.  But at the same time they also hint that there has never been an External attack where the incense was proven to be burned.

notes.title: In-Game Art Release 1
notes.notes:
As is Halloween tradition, we celebrate the countdown towards the release of Tattered Sails by revealing a page from the game every Monday, Wednesday and Friday in the run up to the big day.  The first of these is below.  Please enjoy it, and don't forget to wishlist the title!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40946016/de3227141f3223d91a088de03eba25c92b51ff5d.jpg

Lamps in the shape of marine life are a common sight on most ships.  Sailors believe that by hanging these from the ropes at night the spirits of the drowned who rise up to the deck of the ship will believe they are still underwater.   They will then fly on to pester another ship, or sink back beneath the waves.  Clerical scholars are uncertain as to the legitimacy of this claim, and the money generated by the sale of votive candles and blessed oil to burn in the lamps keeps them from debating the issue too seriously.
